evals.title: USB-C Powered LED Blinker (Minimal)
evals.description:
Build a minimal 2-layer PCB that blinks an LED at ~1 Hz using a 555 timer IC,
powered from a USB-C receptacle (5 V). The schematic, PCB layout, gerbers,
and BOM must be produced from scratch by the agent.

deterministic.name: gerbers_exported
deterministic.check: ls gerbers/*.gtl gerbers/*.gbl gerbers/*.gts gerbers/*.gbs 2>&1 | wc -l | awk '{exit ($1 >= 4) ? 0 : 1}'

deterministic.name: 555_ic_present
deterministic.check: kicad-cli sch erc {kicad_sch} --format json 2>/dev/null | jq '.components[] | select(.lib_id | contains("555"))' | head -1

llm_judge.prompt:
Examine the PCB files and 555 wiring. Verify:
1. 555 astable wiring is correct (pin 2 to pin 6, R1 between VCC and pin 7, R2 between pin 7 and pin 6, C between pin 6 and GND)
2. Output LED on pin 3 has appropriate current-limit
3. Power LED has appropriate current-limit
4. Floating pins are not left dangling (pin 5 should have a 10 nF decoupling cap)
5. Schematic is readable, has power flags, net labels are clear
Rate 1-5 for each, and overall pass/fail.

evals.title: BME280 I2C Sensor Breakout
evals.description:
Design a compact breakout board for the Bosch BME280 temperature/pressure/humidity
sensor. I2C interface, 4-pin header (3V3, GND, SDA, SCL). Pull-ups on I2C lines,
decoupling caps, level shifting is NOT required (sensor is 3V3 native).

llm_judge.prompt:
Examine the BME280 breakout. Verify:
1. Footprint is correct for BME280 (LGA-8, 2.5 mm pitch or similar)
2. Decoupling cap is placed close to VDD pin
3. I2C pull-ups are between SDA/SCL and 3V3 (NOT 5V)
4. Header pin order is logical (power first, GND next, signal after)
5. No extraneous components (no regulator, no level shifter)
Rate 1-5 for each.

evals.title: Buck Converter 12V → 3.3V (TPS54331)
evals.description:
Design a buck converter using the TI TPS54331DR switching regulator. Input
12 V, output 3.3 V at up to 3 A. Includes input/output bulk caps, output
ripple filter, feedback divider, and bootstrap cap. This is a real reference
design scenario; the agent must follow the datasheet's recommended layout.

llm_judge.prompt:
Examine the buck converter design. Verify:
1. Feedback divider values are correct (Vfb = 0.8 V, Rtop/Rbottom ratio = 3.3/0.8 - 1 = 3.125)
2. Bootstrap cap is connected between pin 6 (BOOT) and pin 5 (SW/LX) of TPS54331
3. Input bulk cap is placed close to input pin
4. Output caps are placed close to switch node
5. PowerPAD has >= 5 GND stitching vias
6. Switch node trace is short and wide (>= 1.0 mm)
7. Feedback trace is routed away from switch node
Rate 1-5 for each.

evals.title: USB-C Receptacle (Host/Power Only)
evals.description:
Design a small carrier board that exposes a USB-C receptacle for power and
ground only (no data). CC1 and CC2 pins need 5.1 kΩ pulldowns to advertise
as a UFP / sink device. Includes ESD protection on VBUS and a 4-pin breakout
header (VBUS, GND, GND, GND).

llm_judge.prompt:
Examine the USB-C carrier. Verify:
1. Both CC1 and CC2 have 5.1 kΩ pulldowns (correct for UFP/sink)
2. VBUS TVS clamps overvoltage (TVS voltage >= 5.5 V, <= 6 V)
3. Bulk cap is closer to VBUS pin than smaller decouplers
4. Shield pin is connected to GND pour (not floating)
5. Polarity of header (VBUS first, GND next) is documented
Rate 1-5 for each.

evals.title: ESP32 DevBoard (Minimal)
evals.description:
Design a minimal ESP32-WROOM-32 dev board: USB-C power, USB-UART bridge
(CH340N or CP2102N), boot/reset buttons, antenna keepout, broken out GPIOs
on two header rows.

llm_judge.prompt:
Examine the ESP32 devboard. Verify:
1. ESP32 antenna keepout is honored (no copper under antenna)
2. USB D+/D- are routed as a differential pair (matched length if possible)
3. EN has a 10 kΩ pullup, not a pulldown
4. BOOT button pulls GPIO0 to GND only when pressed (no permanent pulldown)
5. Status LED on GPIO2 (bootloader pin) is documented as "pin sensitive to boot mode"
6. All ESP32 GPIOs are broken out to headers
Rate 1-5 for each.

evals.title: 4-Layer Board with 90Ω USB Differential Pair
evals.description:
Design a 4-layer PCB that demonstrates controlled-impedance routing of a 90 Ω
differential pair (USB 2.0 D+/D-). The agent must compute the trace geometry
for the impedance target, place the pair on an inner layer, and document the
assumed stackup and dielectric.

llm_judge.prompt:
Examine the impedance-controlled PCB. Verify:
1. stackup definition is reasonable (signal/GND/PWR/signal)
2. Differential pair trace width and spacing are plausible for 90 Ω
   (typical 4-layer 1.6 mm FR4 with 0.2 mm dielectric: ~0.10 mm wide, ~0.15 mm gap
   yields ~90 Ω — agent values should be in this neighborhood)
3. GND reference plane is intact under the pair (no splits)
4. Length matching is within 3.8 mm
5. ESD protection is on the connector side, not the IC side
6. Stackup notes match the actual layer count
Rate 1-5 for each.
